In the Mini-Nemesis thread, Empyreon was brought up and I think there is a bunch of relevant stuff bring to the table in support of my theory.

Empyreon is very close to the word Empyrean. From the wiki:

"The Empyrean was thus used as a name for the firmament, and in Christian literature, notably the Divine Comedy, for the dwelling-place of God, the blessed, celestial beings so divine they are made of pure light, and the source of light and creation"

Empyreon looks like he is made of Energy. Its bursting from him. He even damages himself in his AoE, representing the energy disapating from him into offensive output. 

More Christian symbolism is being used here, and if we are going to connect some dots here, that means he could very well be connected to the Cosmic Entity. He could possibly be a part of The Host in some capacity, especially if we are to stick with the Cosmic Entity as God/Creator metaphor.

Speaking of that metaphor, something else occured to me. When talking about all the Odin and Norse mythology symbolism in my Matriarch deck, I compared Odin to the Cosmic Entity there as well. Funny thing, and this is a little simplified, but Odin is a form of the word "Father". Sorta like God for Christianity. Thats not really important itself, but its more evidence for Matriarch could be a part of this as well.

If a great cosmic being had an army, the soldiers could look like Apostate.  If that Great Being had a "Progeny" it could look very different.

Not that I'm sold on the angle, but try this out:

Take the whole Christian arc and turn it a bit askew, make the coming great battle Armageddon and The Host the angels coming to wipe everything out.  Ditch the whole salvation angle, Cosmonautilus eats souls.

In this story Apostate fills his role as being one of the cast out, the one who escapes punishment, probably turned on his friends.  He may be a liar, and evil, but he isn't rebelling against a benevolent/just god, he's weaseled out of active service in the army coming to wipe out everything, and came here hoping to get away from it all to rule his own little insignificant world and do whatever.  (Or maybe the fallen found Earth to be special and he stayed/returned after the mess 

His affiliation is with the host because he has somehow weaseled his way out of trouble and out of direct involvement.

Again I'm not really sold on this, but I have thought about it, esp. when you have "Progeny" coming to Earth alone ahead of the main force.

I could very well see the big bad showing up and Apostate having to pretend he's the loyal servant, or even turning and fighting against it.

Or I could be, and most likely am wrong and it is something incredibly different.
